comparison.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks a robot-gripper stop; PR-1941 fills and removes an evacuated blood tube while an inserted needle remains stable.
comparison.physical_skill: Both use bimanual stabilization, but the candidate counters rotational locknut torque with concentric tools, whereas PR-1941 counterholds a needle holder during axial stopper piercing and tube extraction.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires retained opening across three cycles with bounded drift and nuts retained; PR-1941 requires fill, tube removal and tray placement while needle displacement/tilt or holder release irreversibly fails. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparison.reason: The shared generic counterholding primitive serves different force axes, mechanisms and outcomes: threaded calibration retention versus atraumatic axial tube exchange.
